issue: Is warrantless, long-term (more than 30 days) pole camera surveillance of the plainly visible exterior of a home a search under the Fourth Amendment?

sides.position: Long-term warrantless pole camera surveillance of a home's exterior is a Fourth Amendment search requiring a court order (the Fifth Circuit's holding, though it was tied to a camera that looked over a ten-foot fence)
cases: United States v. Cuevas-Sanchez, 821 F.2d 248 (5th Cir. 1987)

sides.position: Pole camera surveillance of plainly visible areas on public property is not a Fourth Amendment search, regardless of duration
cases: United States v. Tuggle, 4 F.4th 505 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Gonzalez, 328 F.3d 543 (9th Cir. 2003)

this_court: Pole camera surveillance of plainly visible areas of a home from public property is not a search under the Fourth Amendment, even when extended over eighteen months
quote: The answer—and even how to reach it—is the subject of disagreement among our sister circuits and counterparts in state courts.
cite: United States v. Travis Tuggle, 4 F.4th 505 (7th Cir. 2021)
